metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index capabilities <data-dir> <capability> --json`: the provides-index lookup — packages advertising a capability, plus the unusable versions that WOULD have matched it. Read by scripts and agents (PROP-044 §6.5 — a CLI `--json` report is a format plain text; `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/capabilities.rs` (`Envelope`, `Row`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/capabilities_report/`.
The capability the ask named, echoed back verbatim.
How many rows `hits` carries. Bounded by construction and checked at the wire boundary.
Every usable version advertising the capability, in the lookup's deterministic order. Required member: a capability nobody provides writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
Unusable versions that WOULD have matched the requested capability — named, not hidden (PROP-044 §4.5). Absent when there are none (the writer carries `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`).
One version advertising the requested capability.
The version's kind — metadata per PROP-008 §2.3.

The advertised capability string the row matched on (the entry's own spelling, found by prefix overlap with the ask), `null` when the version's `provides` block carries no capabilities at all. The key is always present: the writer's `Option` carries no skip.

One version this build refused to act on, and why — the row every `vibe-index` answering surface carries (`crates/vibe-index/src/index/quarantine.rs`, `Unavailable`). Local to this schema family: `formats/vocabularies.json` does not (yet) carry it, and each of the six report schemas that need it declare their own copy.
The refused version's bare package name.

The reader capabilities of `must_understand` this build lacks, in the record's own order. Required member: a refusal always writes its list, `[]` never occurring in practice today (a row exists exactly because the list is non-empty) but lawful on the wire — the writer has no skip here.
What a person or a script does about it — the fixed two-part text `recipe_for` builds (the explanation with the PROP-044 anchor, then the `fix:` surface).
